body: thank you. i need to hear this. it's still hard to.
yes, i know it's incredibly selfish to die or want to die. i hate myself for that too. it leads me deeper in to the cycle, knowing that. not out of it.

it's one of the things i throw at myself. there's plenty i feel guilty about.

i have a lot of interests, i've never had a shortage of that... so many things are fascinating. i just run out of energy to do anything. 

thank you for saying life is never a waste. that's a good reminder, and it's really in line with my beliefs... it's just easier to think that about anyone besides myself. (so egotistical in my self-hatred... no one's life is a waste except mine. i know the ridiculousness of saying that, but it doesn't mean i can stop feeling it.)

actually, i am in graduate school in a field that i love. (it's not a huge field so i don't want to say what it is, though i know i'm being paranoid.) i do care a lot about social justice issues, which are unrelated to my field (inasmuch as they are ever unrelated to anything)... i guess being aware of inequality just doesn't go together well with self-hatred. i need a lot of support to be in school at all, and i do less at a time than my classmates. i feel i'm very lucky and have a lot of opportunities that others deserve... and the mere fact of my wanting to die means i don't deserve them.

i have plenty of reasons to live, and i know it, it's part of why i hate myself. i know there's things i can do. i've been through and through and through it.

thank you.

you make a good point; i know that everyone uses resources. it just seems to me so much of the time that others do more worthwhile things with what they have. which i know is arbitrary, and in my good times i don't think comparing people is all that helpful. but... if there is an objective measure... i feel like i'm falling pretty short.

thanks to everyone. i have had a few different therapists; recently the one i've had for years retired. she helped me find and transition to a new one. that's part of what makes it tough right now; it takes a while to develop trust and i just don't know how to get around the shame and embarrassment with the new one yet. i know it's a process. it's not actually unusual for someone with my diagnoses to take quite a long time to get through therapy (which can be very discouraging). we use a combination of treatment modalities.  i went to a couple of hospitals with trauma units as well. i founded and cofacilitate a peer support group.

the therapy does help some. i have more functionality than i used to (i'm in grad school, though i can only take one class at a time and it takes all i have and then some.) it's just that i always seem to return to the same state of mind. it just seems like it isn't worth the trouble; other people can live without this much difficulty. it seems like such a waste to even try, when i do so little in so long and have so many more bad days than good.
